name: Coriole Shiraz Lloyd Reserve 2015
text:
## Coriole Shiraz Lloyd Reserve 2015

**The story.** Coriole sits in the hills of [McLaren Vale](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Coriole+Vineyards,+Chaffeys+Road,+McLaren+Vale,+South+Australia,+Australia&t=k), within sight of the sea and less than an hour from Adelaide ([Coriole](https://www.coriole.com/pages/about)). The land was first farmed in the 1840s by Robert and Ann Balderstone, who paid one pound, six shillings and two pence an acre for 157 acres and called it Clark Hill. They grew wheat, ran livestock and a dairy, and probably planted vines soon after; in 1864 Balderstone imported a still. Later Geoffrey Kay, of the Kay Brothers winery, leased the farm, and in 1962 John Snell founded Château Bonne Santé here, described as Australia's first biodynamic winery ([Coriole](https://www.coriole.com/pages/family-history)).

In 1967 an Adelaide doctor, Hugh Lloyd, and his wife Molly bought the property and renamed it Coriole; their 1970 Shiraz won a gold medal at the Adelaide Wine Show. Their son Mark planted [Sangiovese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangiovese) in 1985, now Australia's oldest Sangiovese vineyard, and later brought in Australia's first [Fiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiano_%28grape%29) and [Piquepoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piquepoul), the latter from six cuttings wrapped in wet newspaper and posted from a French nursery. Today the third generation, Peter and Duncan Lloyd, run the estate ([Coriole](https://www.coriole.com/pages/family-history); [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coriole_Vineyards)).

**The vineyard.** Coriole's soils are mainly [terra rossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terra_rossa_%28soil%29), shallow red-brown earth over hard limestone, on the Tapley Hill formation, said to be more than 700 million years old, which gives deeply coloured, structured, long-lived reds. Reds are open-fermented in steel or old wax-lined concrete and hand-plunged, and each block is made separately ([Coriole](https://www.coriole.com/pages/winemaking-viticulture)).

**The wine: Lloyd Reserve.** Lloyd Reserve is Coriole's flagship Shiraz, first released in 1989, from a single old vineyard on deep soil that needs no irrigation. It is matured about 18 months in French oak, typically 25% new, then 18 months or more in bottle before release ([Coriole](https://www.coriole.com/products/2023-lloyd-reserve-shiraz)). The vines were long thought to date from 1919. Then a family member researching a book on Willunga almonds found an 1875 harvest report in the [South Australian Register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Australian_Register) describing "about five acres planted with the red varieties" on "the farm of Mr. Balderston", the same land. Coriole now believes the Lloyd vines were already there in 1875 ([Coriole](https://www.coriole.com/blogs/news/100-year-old-vines)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [South Australia vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/south-australia) says the Barossa's Shiraz "enjoyed an excellent vintage" in 2015, while bushfires in the Adelaide Hills raised fears of smoke taint there.

**What the critics say for 2015.**
- I couldn't find a published critic's score for the 2015 Lloyd Reserve on pages I could read, so I've left critics out rather than guess. For the style, Marcus Ellis of Halliday's Wine Companion, reviewing a recent vintage (96 points), found it "typically black-fruited, with blackberry, plum and olive, coffee, anise, Christmas spices and cured meat", with "intensity, balance and detail" rather than heft ([Coriole](https://www.coriole.com/products/2023-lloyd-reserve-shiraz)).
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.5** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eleven years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2021 to 2035. So it is in its prime, with years to go: expect black fruit, olive, spice and cured meat, with the oak absorbed and the terra rossa structure holding it together. Decant for about an hour.

**Food.** McLaren Vale Shiraz and Mediterranean food go together: braised beef cheeks, a lamb ragù with pappardelle, chargrilled lamb chops with salsa verde, or a cheese board with Coriole's own olives. My pick: slow-cooked lamb shoulder.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Lloyd Reserve, but Coriole's everyday Shiraz is easy to find: BSW Liquor has the 2022 at $29.99, and ZYN the 2023 at $27.60, along with Coriole's [Chenin Blanc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chenin_blanc) at $23.25.

**From the history books**
- **Named for a McLaren.** McLaren Vale was named after either David McLaren, Colonial Manager of the South Australian Company, or John McLaren, who surveyed the area in 1839. The first settlers grew cereal crops, but John Reynell and Thomas Hardy planted vines in 1838, and the forerunners of today's Seaview and Hardys wineries were running by 1850 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Century-old vines.** Some McLaren Vale vines more than 100 years old are still producing ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)), and the region is a member of the Great Wine Capitals of the World network.
- **Between the gulf and the hills.** The region runs 30 km down the coast of the [Gulf St Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_St_Vincent) to the foothills of the [Mount Lofty Ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Lofty_Ranges), with a [Mediterranean climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_climate) of four clear seasons ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Penfolds comes south.** Between 1904 and 1912 [Penfolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds), then the largest winery around Adelaide, bought vineyards in McLaren Vale ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds)).

**Curious details**
- **Where does "Coriole" come from?** The family has competing stories: a blend of letters from Lloyd and Collett, the first partners; the ancient Italian town of [Corioli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corioli), linked to the Roman general [Coriolanus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coriolanus) of Shakespeare's play; or a neighbour's dream of an archway over the gate with "Coriole" written across it ([Coriole](https://www.coriole.com/blogs/news/the-coriole-name)).
- **The Bushing King and Queen.** In 1974 Coriole's Shiraz won Best Wine of the McLaren Vale Wine Show, and Hugh and Molly were crowned Bushing King and Queen; in 1975 Coriole won again ([Coriole](https://www.coriole.com/pages/family-history)).
- **Music among the vines.** The Coriole Music Festival of classical music has been held at the winery since 1999 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coriole_Vineyards)).
